item.title: PAC opens scrutiny of Enemalta over the 2023 power cuts
item.description: Parliament's Public Accounts Committee started on Wednesday examining the National Audit Office report into the widespread power outages Malta experienced in the summer of 2023. The PAC's examination focuses on Enemalta's handling of the outages and will take evidence as part of the audit process. The hearing puts the utility's preparedness and network performance during the heatwave under parliamentary scrutiny.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament's Public Accounts Committee started on Wednesday examining the National Audit Office report into the widespread power outages Malta experienced in the summer of 2023. The PAC's examination focuses on Enemalta's handling of the outages and will take evidence as part of the audit process. The hearing puts the utility's preparedness and network performance during the heatwave under parliamentary scrutiny.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Speaker finds no breach of privilege in Farrugia spat with Labour MP
item.description: Speaker Carmelo Abela ruled that comments by former Malta Employers Association director general Joseph Farrugia against Labour MP Nigel Vella did not constitute a prima facie breach of parliamentary privilege, while urging greater respect in public discourse. The dispute followed Farrugia returning the Ġie ir-Repubblika honour in protest over Yorgen Fenech's acquittal in the Daphne Caruana Galizia murder case.

item.title: Opposition MP alleges the Attorney General's Office was dismantled to shield allies
item.description: Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut told parliament during the Justice Ministry budget estimates debate that the Attorney General's Office has been systematically weakened. He said prosecutor recruitment since 2022 covered only five entry-level posts and 55 trainee lawyers, that the Deputy Attorney General post has been vacant for three years, and criticised the Attorney General's lack of criminal-law background.

item.title: PN launches app to contact MPs and report local issues
item.description: People will soon be able to contact Nationalist Party MPs, suggest parliamentary questions and report issues in their locality through an app due to go live "in the coming days". The party said the tool is intended to bring constituents closer to their representatives.

item.title: 334,865 tax returns still pending between 1999 and 2025
item.description: A National Audit Office report found 334,865 income-tax declarations remain pending, including 260,124 for individuals and 74,741 for companies, with some outstanding for over 25 years. Income tax generated around €3.4 billion in 2025, equal to 51% of government revenue from taxation.

item.title: MDA proposes private traffic officers during construction works
item.description: The Malta Development Association has proposed allowing trained, licensed and insured private traffic management officers to manage traffic flows on roads adjacent to construction sites where public officers are unavailable. The union UĦM said it opposes privatising work that belongs to the public service and has written to the prime minister requesting an urgent meeting.

item.title: Mayors seek full-time option in five-point local government resolution
item.description: Malta's and Gozo's mayors approved a five-point resolution calling for local government reform, including the option for mayors to serve full-time and a larger say in how funding for local councils is allocated. The resolution was adopted at the Local Councils Association's annual mayors conference in Gozo on 13 and 14 November.
item.content:encoded:

The resolution was adopted at the Local Councils Association's annual mayors conference in Gozo on 13 and 14 November.

Sources: Newsbook

item.title: Carabott questions sustainability of Malta's €12 billion public debt
item.description: Nationalist MP Darren Carabott questioned Finance Minister Clyde Caruana on Malta's public debt, which he put at around €12 billion, arguing that borrowing is being used for consumption and wages rather than investment. Caruana defended the sustainability of public finances, noting that recurrent and wage spending is covered by revenue while capital spending is not fully covered.

item.title: 948 children born in Malta to parents from outside the EU in 2025
item.description: Parliamentary figures show 4,338 children were born in Malta in 2025 to parents with one-year residence status, and 948 of them had both parents as citizens of non-EU countries. Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said the residence criterion covers those living in Malta or intending to for at least 12 months.

item.title: Over 2,200 tickets issued to vehicles with foreign plates since 2025
item.description: Parliamentary figures show LESA issued 2,240 tickets to vehicles with foreign number plates between 2025 and the end of October 2026, with the police adding 159, for 2,399 in total. Home Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the figures are drawn from LESA's electronic system.

item.title: Cannabis regulator's revenue stood at €345,000 in 2024 as legal sales began
item.description: Accounts tabled in parliament show the Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis earned €1,561,316 in 2024, up from €1,502,358 in 2023, with the rise attributed to €345,470 received from Cannabis Harm Reduction Associations. The regulator reported 273.5 kilos of legal cannabis sold in 2024 and 2,170 CHRA members, mostly aged between 31 and 40.

item.title: 4,000 urchins bred at Fort San Luċjan for sea repopulation plan
item.description: Around 4,000 urchins have been bred at Fort San Luċjan and are expected to form part of a 50,000-strong release into the sea next year. The programme aims to repopulate Maltese waters and support the recovery of marine habitats.

item.title: The Maltese made 40 million fewer phone calls in 2025
item.description: Maltese made 40 million fewer phone calls in 2025 as online messaging services such as WhatsApp continued to dominate the country's communication market, according to a new Malta Communications Authority report.
